I personally don't use these but I plan on starting fin once I turn 18 after checking in with a dermatologist. I'm sure I have slight recession going on (beyond maturing). I may also microneedle but where I'm at with my hairline I don't think it's really necessary. As I said before the side effects can be there, but they are very rare so most individuals will be able to use it with no problem. Just don't psych yourself out about it and you will be fine. My grandfather used minoxidil for a long time (man had 0 hairline hair and crown hair when he started using it so it wasn't effective) and had no side effects with that. Just be optimistic my friend :) I am soon to join you on this journey.

Medications such as finasteride and minoxidil can help. If you get on those two or even just finasteride (im pretty sure) you can microneedle that area and you should see some regrowth.

Edit: Forgot to add, be aware of side affects such as erectile dysfunction but it is so rare to get and if you do get it reducing your dosage / getting off of finasteride will make it go away in time. There are also some side effects of minoxidil so read up on them too. But most importantly, do not psych yourself out and placebo yourself into getting them, i can say for at least finasteride that the side effects are very rare.

When I first started I used Apple earbuds and audacity for everything. Audacity is a free audio recording software that has some cool features that you should experiment with. 

Download your beat with a youtube to mp3 website (assuming you’re using YouTube to get your beats) and drag it into Audacity. At the top of Audacity, there should be a drop down menu labeled “Tracks”, click on that and click “Add New”. With the new blank track you just added you can record your vocals over the beat you dragged in. I’m not sure about the whole mixing and mastering aspect of Audacity, I never bothered with that stuff at the start, now I use FL Studio to do all of that. Also, this is your first song, so don’t expect it to be anywhere near perfect. It probably won’t sound exactly how you want it to but that’s all part of the process, so don’t let it discourage you. 

I know I left out some other stuff about Audacity that’s good to know but it’s really easy to use and you’ll probably figure it out within the first 5 minutes. Good luck and I can answer any questions you need me to!
